paper_a.title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization

metadata.description: Paper B (Loshchilov-Hutter) extends Paper A's Adam by decoupling weight decay from the gradient-based moment estimates, producing AdamW. Paper B explicitly cites Adam as prior work (its AP246.4 is Kingma-Ba's Algorithm 1) and proves three propositions characterizing when L2 regularization and weight decay coincide; the new contribution is the AdamW algorithm and its theoretical/empirical motivation. Relation is EXT rather than BI because A's Adam and B's AdamW are demonstrably non-equivalent updates (Proposition 2).

matches.explanation: Paper A's Adam algorithm (AP214.1) is precisely the 'Adam (with L2 regularization)' baseline of Paper B (AP246.4), which is explicitly tagged origin=external with citation 'Kingma and Ba 2015'. Same pseudocode structure: bias-corrected first/second moments and the update theta_t <- theta_{t-1} - alpha * hat{m}_t / (sqrt(hat{v}_t) + epsilon). Paper B uses it as the L2-regularized baseline against which AdamW is compared.

AdamW (AP246.2) modifies Adam (AP214.1) by decoupling weight decay from the moment estimates: instead of folding lambda*theta into g_t before forming m_t, v_t, the term -eta_t * lambda * theta_{t-1} is added directly to the parameter update line. Same adaptive-moment skeleton (m_t, v_t, hat-corrections) but a different regularization placement; Paper B's Proposition 2 proves the two are not equivalent for any choice of L2 coefficient when the preconditioner is non-scalar.

Composite L2-vs-L2 algorithm-step alignment for the parent algorithms (Adam vs AdamW). Initialization (ASP214.1 ~ ASP246.5), main loop / gradient sampling (ASP214.2-3 ~ ASP246.6 first half), first-moment update (ASP214.4 ~ ASP246.6), second-moment update (ASP214.5 ~ ASP246.6), bias correction (ASP214.6-7 ~ ASP246.7), parameter update (ASP214.8 ~ ASP246.8 -- where AdamW differs by adding -eta_t * lambda * theta_{t-1} as a decoupled term), return (ASP214.9 ~ ASP246.9). The decoupled-decay step in ASP246.8 is the substantive deviation.

Biased first-moment estimate m_t (EMA of gradients) is defined identically in Paper B's algorithm steps but never broken out as a separate definition node. The concept is preserved (used inside ASP246.6) but no L1 definition node corresponds; effectively part of the AdamW algorithm node.
Biased second raw moment estimate v_t. Same as DP214.3 -- conceptually present in AdamW (ASP246.6) but not extracted as a standalone definition in Paper B.
Bias-corrected hat{m}_t, hat{v}_t. Reused in AdamW (line in ASP246.7) but not given a dedicated definition in Paper B.
Stochastic objective f(theta). Implicit in Paper B's setting (it minimizes a batch loss f_t under various optimizers) but not given a formal definition node.
Stochastic gradient g_t. Used everywhere in Paper B (e.g., ASP246.6) but not defined as its own node.
Effective stepsize Delta_t and signal-to-noise ratio. Paper A-specific analytical artifact (Section 2.1); Paper B does not analyze the per-step magnitude in this form.
Exponentially weighted infinity norm u_t (used by AdaMax). AdaMax is a Paper-A-only variant; Paper B has no L_infinity analogue.
Auxiliary constant gamma = beta_1 / sqrt(beta_2). Used only in Paper A's regret-bound analysis (Theorem 4.1), which Paper B does not redo.
Closed form v_t = (1-beta_2) sum beta_2^{t-i} g_i^2 (Paper A eq.1). Internal to Paper A's bias-correction derivation; Paper B reuses bias correction without re-deriving it.
Expected v_t vs true second moment (Paper A eq.4). Same scope as EP214.1 -- internal Paper A derivation step.
AdaMax recursion u_t = max(beta_2 u_{t-1}, |g_t|). Paper-A-specific.
Effective-stepsize bounds for Adam. Paper-A-specific upper bound on |Delta_t|.
Bounded gradients/iterates assumption. Used only by Paper A's regret bound; Paper B has no convergence theorem.
Decaying schedules alpha_t = alpha/sqrt(t), beta_{1,t} = beta_1 lambda^{t-1}. Used by Paper A's regret bound only.
AdaMax algorithm (Paper-A-only variant). Paper B has no L_infinity-norm Adam variant.
Temporal averaging extension (Polyak-Ruppert-style EMA of theta). Paper B does not include parameter-iterate averaging.
Lemma 10.3 (sum of g_{t,i}^2/t bound). Internal scaffolding of Paper A's regret proof.
Lemma 10.4 (hat{m}_t^2/sqrt(t hat{v}_t) bound). Internal scaffolding of Paper A's regret proof.
Adam regret bound (Theorem 4.1/10.5). Paper B has no convergence/regret analysis -- it focuses on generalization-via-regularization, not online-convex-optimization rates.
Corollary 4.2 (R(T)/T -> 0). Same scope as TP214.1 -- Paper-A-only.
Derivation of bias correction for v_t. Paper-A-only theoretical content.
Derivation of AdaMax. Paper-A-only theoretical content.
Proof of Lemma 10.3 by induction on T. Internal to Paper A's regret-bound proof chain.
Proof of Lemma 10.4. Internal to Paper A's regret-bound proof chain.
Proof of Theorem 10.5 (Adam regret bound). Paper B has no analogous proof.
Proof of Corollary 4.2. Paper-A-only.

Both papers state a stochastic-optimization problem, but at different abstraction levels: Paper A poses the generic problem of minimizing E[f(theta)] from noisy gradients; Paper B's problem is more applied -- find a regularization scheme for adaptive gradient methods that closes the generalization gap to SGD-with-momentum on deep-network image classification. The latter narrows A's setting to deep networks and adds a generalization-gap criterion. Aligned as analogous because they share the optimization-of-stochastic-objective core but differ in framing and goal.
Weight decay (Hanson-Pratt 1988). Paper A does not discuss weight decay or L2 regularization as an explicit definition; Paper B's central object.
L2 regularization. Paper-B-specific definition; Paper A's experimental section briefly mentions L2-regularized logistic regression but does not define the concept formally.
Schedule multiplier eta_t. Paper-B-specific design choice introduced to allow cosine annealing and warm restarts; Paper A uses only alpha_t = alpha/sqrt(t).
Adaptive gradient algorithm with preconditioner M_t. Paper-B-specific abstraction (used in Propositions 2-3) covering Adam, AdaGrad, etc.; Paper A does not formalize this generic class.
Normalized weight decay lambda_norm. Paper-B-specific reparameterization for budget-invariant tuning.
Decoupled weight-decay update equation theta_{t+1} = (1-lambda) theta_t - alpha grad. Paper-B-specific.
SGDW (SGD with momentum and decoupled weight decay). Paper-B-specific; Paper A has no SGD-with-decoupled-decay variant.
AdamWR (AdamW + warm restarts + normalized weight decay). Paper-B-specific composite algorithm.
Proposition 1: weight decay equals L2 regularization for standard SGD. Paper-B-specific theoretical contribution.
Proposition 2: weight decay differs from L2 regularization for adaptive gradients. The pivotal result motivating AdamW; no counterpart in Paper A.
Proposition 3: weight decay equals scale-adjusted L2 regularization for fixed preconditioner. Paper-B-specific.
Proof of Proposition 1. Paper-B-specific.
Proof of Proposition 2. Paper-B-specific.
Proof of Proposition 3. Paper-B-specific.
